To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a high-resolution genetic map was developed for the domestic cat genome using the Illumina 60K SNP array, which was used to anchor a substantially more contiguous new genome assembly (v8.0).
we developed the longest linkage map of any mammal to date and used it to order the scaffolds of a substantially more contiguous draft assembly of the domestic cat (Felis catis v8.0).
a high-resolution genetic map of the domestic (house) cat genome has been constructed, and that the map was used to anchor a new, substantially more contiguous genome assembly.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the production of a high-quality genome assembly and map for the domestic cat, which will be a valuable resource for the domestic cat breeding and biomedical research communities, as well as comparative genomicists.

the development of a high-resolution genetic map for the domestic cat, and the use of that map to anchor the latest domestic cat genome assembly and to describe features and patterns of recombination.
the construction of high-density genetic and physical maps of domestic cat genome.

the high-resolution SNP linkage map is the most valuable tool in the cat genomics toolbox.
the new linkage map is an excellent tool for ordering and orienting the scaffolds of a high-quality domestic cat genome assembly, and will be useful in future GWAS studies.

the domestic cat has one of the largest genome assemblies of any mammal, with the longest genetic map, and that the genome assembly is now sufficiently contiguous that it is likely to be useful to the community of cat genetic researchers and breeders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have produced the most accurate genome assembly to date for the domestic cat, which should enable more accurate identification of genes underlying traits of interest, and facilitate more accurate comparative analyses between cats and other species, including humans.

this high-resolution linkage map provides the most detailed view to date of the genetic map of the domestic feline genome, and that the map is a valuable tool for future genetic mapping studies and the interpretation of GWAS results.
the high-resolution linkage map presented here is a powerful resource to support the interpretation of GWAS, and for anchoring future domestic cat genome assemblies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high-density genetic map can serve as a powerful tool for anchoring a genome assembly, and for validating and improving the accuracy of the resulting map and assembly.
the high-resolution map we describe here will be useful for anchoring future domestic cat genome assemblies, and for anchoring and validating the assembly of the genome from any other cat species.
high-resolution genetic maps are a valuable complement to physical maps, and that they can provide important insights into genome organization, recombination landscapes, and structural variation.
